system.description:
Your companion isn't summoned — it's built, bolted, and wound by hand, and it remembers every repair you've ever made to it.

  • Construct Companion (1st): Build a Small construct companion (d8 Hit Dice equal to your level; AC 14, +1 per four levels; attack bonus equal to the Martial Base to Hit for a level equal to its HD, to a maximum of 24th; saves of half your level, minimum +1; immune to poison, disease and sleep).
  • Its attacks deal +1 damage per four Artificer levels.
  • It acts on your initiative and follows spoken commands.
  • Commanding it is part of your turn and costs nothing; without a command it takes no action.
  • Example chassis — Guardian: Move 30ft, slam (1d8), +1 AC while adjacent to you; Scout: Move 40ft, climb 20ft, bite (1d6), Advantage on Perception; Striker: Move 30ft, blade arm (1d10).
  • If destroyed, it can be rebuilt over a full rest with materials.
  • Modular Chassis (3rd): Swap the construct's weapon mount (Blade Arm, Cannon Arm) or utility mount (Grasping Claw, Lantern Core, Climbing Legs, Alarm Core) during any rest, no cost.
  • Reinforced Plating (5th): The construct's AC increases by 2 and it gains Resistance 5 to one damage type of your choice, set at creation.
  • Independent Action (7th): The construct can act on its own initiative count and no longer requires your command each round to take a basic action (attack nearest enemy, defend, retrieve).
  • Lasting Work: True Construct (10th): Spend a full day and appropriate materials to permanently upgrade your companion's chassis — each upgrade gives it 2 more Hit Dice and one permanent magical enhancement (flight, invisibility on command, a breath weapon dealing elemental damage, or similar), GM-approved. It can take one upgrade at 10th level and a second at 20th; replacing an enhancement later adds no Hit Dice.
  • Magnum Opus: The Masterwork Automaton (24th): Your companion undergoes a final transformation — +4 HD, it gains a second attack, and it can cast one Wizard spell of 3rd level or lower, chosen when the Opus is finished, whenever you spend 2 Ingenuity Points per spell level. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and rare materials the GM determines.

Known Chassis Mods

  • Blade Arm (weapon mount) — 1d8 slashing melee attack
  • Cannon Arm (weapon mount) — 1d6 force damage, 30ft range
  • Piercer Arm (weapon mount) — 1d6 piercing melee attack, ignores 2 points of the target's armour
  • Grasping Claw (utility mount) — Advantage on grapple attempts; can retrieve small objects at your command
  • Lantern Core (utility mount) — Sheds light in a 30ft radius, shutterable on command
  • Climbing Legs (utility mount) — Climb speed equal to normal move speed
  • Alarm Core (utility mount) — The construct cannot be surprised while active and alerts you the instant it's triggered or attacked
  • Vocal Mimic (utility mount) — The construct can repeat up to one sentence of speech it has heard, in the speaker's own voice
  • Reinforced Chassis (passive) — +2 to the construct's current HD total
  • Balanced Frame (passive) — The construct gains +1 to its AC
  • Recall Ward (passive) — You can call the construct to your side from anywhere within 1 mile with a spoken word
  • Storage Cavity (utility mount) — The construct has a hidden compartment holding up to 4 slots' worth of items
  • Mounts and passives: a construct carries one weapon mount and one utility mount, swapped during a rest (see Modular Chassis).
  • Passives are installed during a rest and count as known options.
  • A construct holds one passive, plus one more at 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th level.
  • Each passive can be installed only once, and removing and reinstalling Reinforced Chassis adds no further Hit Dice.

Designing a Custom Mount

  • Benchmark: A weapon mount should deal damage in line with a simple one-handed weapon (1d6-1d8), scaled by attack type rather than by size.
  • A utility mount should grant one clear non-combat capability (movement, detection, storage, communication) rather than a combat bonus — if it starts granting damage or AC, it's a weapon mount or passive instead.
  • A passive mod should be a small, permanent numeric bump (+1 to +2) to one stat, never a whole new capability.
